subject: math

entries: The sampling distribution of the mean shrinks as n grows: sample means cluster around the true mean, and as n grows from 2 to 25 the distribution of those means gets taller and narrower, because the spread shrinks by root n.
slots.label: The sampling distribution shrinks as n grows
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Hypothesis testing: the p-value decides against α: state H0 and H1, shade the tail beyond the observed statistic to read the p-value, and reject H0 exactly when that p-value falls below alpha = 0.05.
slots.label: State H0 and H1, then compare p with alpha
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The p-value trap: it is not P(H₀ is true): repeat the test 100 times while H0 is true and about 3 repeats land in the extreme tail - that count of repeats is all the p-value of 0.03 says.
slots.label: The p-value trap: not the probability H0 is true
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Type I and Type II errors: the two ways to be wrong: lay reality across the top and the decision down the side - rejecting a true null is the Type I false alarm capped by alpha, and accepting a false null is the Type II missed signal fought with power.
slots.label: Type I and Type II errors: the two ways to be wrong
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The distribution of a statistic, such as the sample mean, over many repeated samples of the same size: the sample means cluster around the true mean, with standard deviation sigma / root n.
slots.label: Sampling distribution
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A procedure that states a null hypothesis H0 and an alternative H1, then rejects H0 when the observed data would be sufficiently surprising if H0 were true.
slots.label: Hypothesis test
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The probability, computed assuming H0 is true, of getting data at least as extreme as the data observed: if H0 were true, a p-value of 0.03 means 3% of experiments would give data this extreme.
slots.label: p-value
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The threshold alpha, often 0.05, fixed before the test: reject H0 when the p-value is smaller than alpha. Alpha also caps the probability of a Type I error.
slots.label: Significance level
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Rejecting a true null hypothesis - a false alarm. Its probability is alpha, the significance level chosen in advance.
slots.label: Type I error
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Accepting a false null hypothesis - a missed signal. Its probability is beta, and the power of the test, 1 - beta, is the chance of avoiding it.
slots.label: Type II error
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
